terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, with two accusatives (whom and what)
terms.comment: The person taught and the thing taught are both accusative: puerōs elementa docet. It is also “show, inform” (see explain).
Literally “take the roughness out”: to educate, more formal than docēre.

evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. ērudiō: with īnstituere
terms.comment: To ground someone in something, to train; its everyday senses are “set up, begin, decide”.

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation: aliquem aliquā rē
terms.comment: To furnish someone, as with tools, with knowledge or rules; the person is the object and the subject in the ablative.

phrases.latin: fās est et ab hoste docērī
phrases.english: it is right to be taught even by an enemy

phrases.latin: Praeceptor sedet in cathedrā; discipulī in subselliīs; ille docet, hī discunt.
phrases.english: The teacher sits in his chair, the pupils on the benches; he teaches, they learn.

sources: Lewis & Short: doceo · Lewis & Short: erudio · Lewis & Short: instituo
